advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile check_ac_compute with the strict evaluate_plan_clarity floor (or document why check-ac intentionally stays loose) so the two AC gates cannot disagree.
evidence: gates.py:165-168 `floor = evaluate_plan_clarity(description)` / `if score >= threshold and floor.passes:`
gates.py:74 check_ac still `n = _count_ac_reset(_ticket_text(state))`
gates.py:60 `if found and ln.startswith("- ["): count += 1` (loose)
_plan_clarity.py:17 `_CHECKBOX_RE = re.compile(r"^- \[(?: |x|X)\](?:[ \t]+(.*))?$")` (strict) — `- [x]done` fails fullmatch, `- [x]done` still counts under _count_ac_reset
tests/unit/test_clarity_floor.py `_assert_both_fail`/`_assert_both_pass` only exercise clarity-check and p1, never check_ac_compute, so the divergence is untested
advisory.finding: clarity-check now enforces the strict evaluate_plan_clarity floor (requiring canonical `- [ ]`/`- [x]` markers, non-empty joined items, and no sentinels), but the sibling `check_ac_compute` still uses the loose `_count_ac_reset` (matches any line `startswith('- [')`). A plan with e.g. `- [x]done` (missing marker whitespace) or a whitespace-only item now FAILS clarity-check yet PASSES check-ac, a new inconsistency between two gates that previously shared AC-counting semantics.
scenarios: A ticket with a non-canonical checkbox marker passes check-ac gate but fails clarity-check gate, yielding contradictory readiness signals.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the `_count_ac_items` docstring to reflect delegation to evaluate_plan_clarity and note it no longer matches `_count_ac_reset` exactly.
evidence: det_floor.py:159-160 `(reset on the next "## " heading). Mirrors gates._count_ac_reset so the DET / floor shares the exact vocabulary of the standalone check_ac gate.`
det_floor.py:161 `return len(evaluate_plan_clarity(text).ac_items)`
_plan_clarity.py:16 `_H2_RE = re.compile(r"^##[ \t]+(.+?)[ \t]*$")` requires exact heading match, unlike `_count_ac_reset`'s `ln.lower().startswith("## acceptance criteria")`
advisory.finding: The `_count_ac_items` docstring still asserts it 'Mirrors gates._count_ac_reset so the DET floor shares the exact vocabulary of the standalone check_ac gate', but the body now delegates to `evaluate_plan_clarity`, which uses stricter checkbox/heading matching than `_count_ac_reset`. The stated invariant is now false and misleading.
scenarios: A maintainer trusts the docstring and assumes check-ac and the DET floor count AC items identically.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope suppression to the sentinel's own clause rather than the whole line so a co-located suppression word cannot mask a genuine unresolved sentinel.
evidence: _plan_clarity.py:83-84 `if _SUPPRESSION_RE.search(visible): return None`
_plan_clarity.py:28-31 suppression words include `no|zero|remove|delete|reject|forbid|without` and `must not`

tests/unit/test_clarity_floor.py `test_same_line_removal_and_negation_assertions_suppress_sentinel` codifies whole-line suppression as intended, but only for lines where the sentinel IS the negated subject
advisory.finding: `_SUPPRESSION_RE.search(visible)` suppresses sentinel detection for the ENTIRE line, so a genuine unresolved value co-located with any suppression word is silently missed — e.g. `Remove old flags; backend = TBD` or `must not regress; status: FIXME` reports no sentinel even though `backend = TBD` is a real unresolved assignment.
scenarios: A plan line that both removes something AND leaves a real value unresolved passes the floor, letting an unresolved execution choice through.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize sentinel line numbering (e.g. count within the description) so evidence line numbers are meaningful and consistent across clarity-check and P1.
evidence: det_floor.py:201 `f"{item.section} line {item.line_number}: {item.line}"`
det_floor.py:152-153 `return f"{self.title}\n\n{self.description}"` (plan_text prepends title + blank line)
gates.py:165 clarity feeds `description` only to evaluate_plan_clarity
advisory.finding: Sentinel evidence reports `line {line_number}` computed from the parsed text, which differs by surface: p1_readiness_shape parses `ctx.plan_text` (title + blank line + description, offsetting numbers by 2), while clarity-check parses description-only. The reported line number therefore does not correspond to the author's description for p1 and disagrees between the two surfaces.
scenarios: An operator reading p1 evidence jumps to the reported line in the description and finds the wrong line.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion on the failing `p1.finding` content (defect category names, evidence lines, suggested_fix) for each of the three defect classes.
evidence: `_assert_both_fail` asserts only: `assert p1.status == "fail"` / `assert p1.blocked` (tests/unit/test_clarity_floor.py:47-49)
The diff adds category-specific finding text in det_floor.py:182-221 (`defects`, `evidence`, `fixes` for the three cases)
ABSENCE: search for `empty_ac_items` / finding-content assertions finds hits only in src/, none in tests/unit/test_clarity_floor.py
det_floor.py:172-178 adds `"empty_ac_items": len(floor.empty_ac_items)` and `"sentinel_assignments": len(floor.sentinel_assignments)` to `cov`
Neither `_assert_both_pass` nor `_assert_both_fail` inspects `p1.coverage`
ABSENCE: `empty_ac_items` appears only in src/ per search, never in the test file
advisory.finding: The new structured `finding` emitted by `p1_readiness_shape` on failure — the defect categorization (`no standard ## Acceptance Criteria checklist` vs `empty Acceptance Criteria items` vs `unresolved sentinel assignments`), the per-category `evidence` lines, and the composed `suggested_fix` — is asserted by no test. Tests only check `p1.status == 'fail'` and `p1.blocked`. A regression that reports the wrong defect category or drops evidence would pass every test.
merged_from: The new P1 `coverage` fields `empty_ac_items` and `sentinel_assignments` (added in det_floor.py:172-178) are never asserted. No test verifies these counts are populated correctly, so a regression zeroing or mis-counting them (e.g. off-by-one in `empty_ac_items.append(len(ac_items))`) is undetectable via the coverage record the attestation relies on.
scenarios: A refactor that misroutes an empty-AC failure into the sentinel branch (or vice-versa) still emits status=fail and passes all tests, shipping a wrong/misleading operator-facing finding.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the empty-AC and sentinel failure tests, assert on `p1.finding`, e.g. `assert 'empty Acceptance Criteria items' in p1.finding['finding']` and that `p1.finding['evidence']` names the offending item/line; for the no-AC case assert the `no standard ## Acceptance Criteria checklist` phrasing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a failure case combining ≥2 defect categories (e.g. empty AC item plus a sentinel in Approach) asserting both appear in the composed finding/suggested_fix.
evidence: det_floor.py:212-213 `", ".join(defects)` and det_floor.py:220 `"; ".join(fixes)` compose multiple categories
All failure tests set exactly one defective section (single parametrized `line`/`item`), never two categories together
advisory.finding: Multi-defect composition is untested. When a plan simultaneously has an empty AC item AND a sentinel assignment, `finding['finding']` comma-joins defects and `suggested_fix` semicolon-joins fixes; no test exercises more than one defect category at a time, so the joining logic and ordering are unverified.
scenarios: A plan with both an empty AC item and a sentinel in Approach — the combined message path is never executed by tests.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Version/document the `clarity-check` accepted-input narrowing (exact heading + strict checkbox + empty-item/sentinel rejection) with a CHANGELOG/release-notes entry, or relax the heading/checkbox matcher to preserve the previously-accepted forms.
evidence: gates.py:164-168 new: `score = _clarity_score(...)` then `floor = evaluate_plan_clarity(description)` and `if score >= threshold and floor.passes:` (was `ac_count = _count_ac_reset(description)` / `if score >= threshold and ac_count >= 1:` in the diff)

PlanClarityFloor.passes: `return bool(self.ac_items) and not self.empty_ac_items and not self.sentinel_assignments` — adds two NEW fail modes beyond the old `>= 1` count

Consumers of the changed gate: src/rebar/_lib_gates.py:54 `gates.clarity_check_compute(...)` (the `rebar.clarity_check` library fn), src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:207 `clarity_check` MCP tool, CLI `clarity-check` (docs/cli-reference.md:57)
No CHANGELOG.md/release-notes entry accompanies the diff; CHANGELOG.md:11-15 latest release states 'no breaking changes'

Diff tests confirm the tightening is intended: tests/unit/test_clarity_floor.py `test_sentinel_value_positions_fail_both_surfaces`, `test_nonstandard_checkbox_marker_does_not_satisfy_the_floor`, `test_fully_joined_whitespace_only_ac_item_fails_both_surfaces`
advisory.finding: The public `clarity-check` gate (`clarity_check_compute`) narrows its accepted input unversioned: the pass predicate changed from `ac_count >= 1` (loose `_count_ac_reset`: prefix-matched `## acceptance criteria` heading + any `- [` line) to `floor.passes` (exact-casefold `acceptance criteria` heading, strict `- [ ]`/`- [x]` checkbox needing whitespace, and new rejection of empty joined AC items and unresolved sentinels). Descriptions that previously PASSED — e.g. a qualified `## Acceptance Criteria (MVP)` heading, a `- [ ]text` item, or an item naming a TBD/TODO sentinel — now FAIL, changing the exit code / verdict for existing tickets.
scenarios: A ticket that scored >= threshold and filed criteria under `## Acceptance Criteria (target state)` passed `rebar clarity-check` before; it now fails because the heading is no longer an exact match.
A ticket with `- [ ]item` (no space after the marker) or a criterion whose only content is `TBD` passed before and now fails.
